findings.title: Failed device-limit check is cached, allowing bypass
findings.body: In AnonDeviceService.tagDeviceUI in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go the localCache entry is set with SetDefault before calling CreateOrUpdateDevice. If the DB call fails with ErrDeviceLimitReached for a new device, the cache entry remains for ~29 minutes. The next request for the same deviceID hits the cache early-return nil path and authenticates successfully, so the device limit denies only the first request and then allows the device. Cache should only be populated after a successful store, or evicted on failure.

findings.title: Count-then-insert device limit is racy
findings.body: In AnonDBStore.CreateOrUpdateDevice in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go the code does CountDevices, then if count >= limit calls updateDevice, otherwise does an upsert, in separate sessions with no transaction or lock. Concurrent anonymous logins can all observe count < limit and all insert, exceeding the configured limit. A hard limit needs atomic enforcement e.g. transaction with locking, serialized insertion, or post-insert trimming.

findings.title: Unchanged UPDATE reports limit-reached for existing devices
findings.body: In AnonDBStore.updateDevice in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database.go rowsAffected==0 is mapped unconditionally to ErrDeviceLimitReached. On MySQL an UPDATE that sets columns to their existing values affects 0 rows without CLIENT_FOUND_ROWS, and similarly any no-op heartbeat can return 0. An existing device that is still within the 30-day window but sends identical client_ip/user_agent would then be treated as over-limit and denied authentication, even though updates for existing devices should succeed when limited.

findings.title: Anonymous tagging moved to synchronous auth path
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/client.go Anonymous.Authenticate previously tagged the device in a background goroutine with a 2-minute timeout and never blocked login. It now calls TagDevice synchronously with the request context, which does CountDevices plus Insert/Update. Every cache-miss anonymous authentication now pays two DB round-trips on the login path, increasing p99 login latency and making anonymous logins fail or hang when the DB is slow, and tying tagging lifetime to request cancellation.

findings.title: Constructor signature change breaks DI / callers
findings.body: In pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/impl.go ProvideAnonymousDeviceService was changed from taking anonStore anonstore.AnonStore to taking sqlStore db.DB and internally calling ProvideAnonDBStore(sqlStore, cfg.AnonymousDeviceLimit), while ProvideAnonDBStore now requires an int64 deviceLimit. Any wire/fx provider set or test that supplies AnonStore or calls ProvideAnonDBStore with one argument no longer resolves; a plain int64 cannot be auto-wired. This is a breaking provider contract that needs wire set updates or a separate config-injected constructor.

findings.title: No test that existing device can update after limit reached
findings.body: TestIntegrationBeyondDeviceLimit in pkg/services/anonymous/anonimpl/anonstore/database_test.go only verifies that a second distinct deviceID is rejected with ErrDeviceLimitReached when limit=1. It never verifies the intended allowed path: re-tagging the first existing device after the limit is reached should succeed via updateDevice. The negative-cache bug and the unchanged-row bug above would not be caught by the current tests.
